screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
How many years' experience do you have as a project engineer?
Have you led site teams, including subcontractors, to install or commission industrial machinery, process equipment or automated handling systems?
What was your role on your most recent installation or commissioning project?
candidates.content_text:
Project Engineer - Industrial Machinery
 Melbourne | Permanent full-time | National site travel
 Own the project from order to sign-off
About the company
 Our client is the Australian arm of a German family-owned global manufacturer of industrial laundry systems. They design and build large automated laundry lines for healthcare, hospitality and commercial laundries. The Australian team is small, so your work will be visible every day.
 The role
 You'll be the single accountable owner of every equipment project in Australia, from estimate through installation and commissioning to signed customer acceptance. You'll also manage warranty claims and technical complaints with the factory in Germany.
 What you'll do
 - Work with Sales on estimates, then build the project plan, budget, resources and site schedule
 - Lead installation teams on site: company technicians, subcontractors, casual labour and visiting specialists from Germany
 - Own site safety: risk assessments, SWMS, permits, isolations and contractor inductions under an ISO 45001 system
 - Commission and document every safety function, close out punch lists, and obtain signed customer acceptance
 - Hand over each project in writing to the service team
 - Report weekly on progress, cost, risks and customer issues
 - Manage warranty and complaint cases through to a documented root cause
 Career path
 - Year 1: project delivery and warranty management
 - Year 2: first point of technical contact, using fault data to drive fixes with Germany
 - Year 3+: Product & Application Specialist, advising customers and Sales on plant layout and training others
 About you
 - Degree in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics Engineering
 - Experience leading site teams and subcontractors to install and commission industrial machinery, process equipment or automated handling systems
 - Able to read mechanical and electrical schematics, with working knowledge of PLC-controlled systems preferably 
 - Strong knowledge of site safety under Australian WHS legislation
 - Clear, disciplined written communication
 - Current driver's licence and comfortable with frequent interstate travel, including multi-week site periods
 Highly regarded: materials handling or industrial machinery experience, warranty claims management, and project management training or certification.
What's on offer
 - Real ownership in a small, growing team
 - The backing of a global family-owned manufacturer with a long engineering heritage
 - Large, complex installations across healthcare, hospitality and commercial laundry
 - Factory training in Germany and a defined path to Product & Application Specialist

candidates.content_text:
ABOUT US
Ertech is a proudly employee-owned Australian civil and electrical construction company, delivering high-quality services across the Transport, Infrastructure, Resources, and Defence sectors. We partner with clients in both the public and private sectors, including state and federal governments. Since our humble beginnings in 1981, we’ve built a strong reputation for the quality of our work and the long-term relationships we foster — all driven by our core values of collaboration, courage, and authenticity.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We are currently recruiting for an experienced Project Engineer to join our team in NSW, taking the lead on QA/QC requirements across our long-term construction projects. This role will involve travel between our Sydney-based project sites.
As the Project Engineer, you will play a key role in managing quality assurance and quality control activities, ensuring project requirements and standards are met. You will work closely with project teams to maintain quality processes, drive continuous improvement and embed a strong culture of quality and excellence across our projects.
Other key responsibilities include, but not limited to:
- Report to the Project Manager and client on all QA/QC matters, while managing and motivating a team of Quality Engineers
- Produce the Quality Management Plans and related Quality Management tools, including Work Packs, Inspection & Test Plans, and Check Sheets in readiness for site construction, installations and field inspections
- Ensure Project teams complete all required QA/QC surveillance and documentation to the applicable project requirements and standards
- Understand the non-conformance process and liaise with the client and the project teams to develop corrective and preventative actions to mitigate reoccurrence.
- Provide in house training to Project team members on Quality documentation and surveillance activities.
- Ensure the Contractor's and vendor's quality records and MDR's are compiled in a progressive manner throughout the course of the works
 To be successful, you will have experience and demonstrate capability in the following:
- Minimum 5+ years of relevant experience in a Quality Engineer or similar role on construction projects.
- Strong technical knowledge surrounding Civil and Electrical Engineering scopes.
- Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Bachelor in Civil Engineering or similar qualification (desirable).
- Ability to obtain a National Police Clearence.
- MUST hold relevant Australian working rights.
WHY JOIN ERTECH?
At Ertech, we’re committed to investing in our people and creating a workplace where you can thrive. Here’s what you can look forward to: 
- Competitive remuneration
- Metro-based project – enjoy the benefit of being home every night
- Full-time position offering stability and annual leave entitlements
- Supportive, team-oriented culture where collaboration and respect are valued 
- Play a key role in shaping the growth and success of our projects
- Career development and progression opportunities, annual performance development plans.
- Access to great benefits, including: 
- Discounted Private Health Insurance (HBF & Medibank)
- Annual flu vaccinations 
- Novated leasing options through Paywise
- Service recognition and milestone rewards 
- Employee Referral Program incentives 
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family.
OUR CULTURE
At Ertech, our people are fundamental to our success. We're focused on creating an inclusive workplace, with the right people in the right roles, who are engaged, empowered, and appropriately rewarded. Ertech will provide you with the chance to be a part of great team, meet new people and gain experience with an industry leader who puts safety first. 
DIVERSITY & INCLUSION
We value the unique backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives of all people and actively encourage applications from First Nations peoples, all genders, culturally and linguistically diverse individuals, people with disability, LGBTQIA+ community members, and veterans of the Australian Defence Force.
Ertech is a proud Veteran Employment supporter. We recognise the valuable skills and leadership that veterans bring to our industry and welcome their applications at all levels of the business. Even if you don’t meet every requirement listed, we encourage you to apply and bring your strengths to our team.
HOW TO APPLY
Click "Apply" on this job advertisement, which will direct you to Ertech's application portal. Simply follow the steps outlined on the portal to complete your application.
This is an incredible opportunity! If you are looking for a position in an environment in which you can flourish whilst building your career, there is no better time to join the Ertech Team than now!

Are you looking to kick start your career in Concreting? Obtain a Nationally Recognised Qualification and valuable experience in Concreting with an Apprenticeship at Lake Mac Council!
ABOUT THE JOB
This 2-year Concreting Traineeship is the perfect opportunity to kick-start your career while making a real difference in the Lake Macquarie community. As a Concreting Trainee, you'll gain hands-on experience in a variety of concreting and construction activities, including footpaths, cycleways, formwork, steel fixing, traffic calming devices, kerb and channel construction (by hand and machine), driveways, drainage pits, pedestrian ramps, median islands and pedestrian refuges.
Through a combination of on-the-job training and formal study, you'll develop the practical skills and industry knowledge needed for a successful career in concreting and civil construction, while learning to safely operate tools, equipment and machinery.
This exciting position will see you:
- Assist with a broad range of concreting and civil construction works, including maintenance and renewal projects.
- Operate small plant and equipment under supervision.
- Learn and apply concreting techniques, including screeding and finishing concrete across a variety of projects.
- Work collaboratively as part of a skilled and supportive team.
- Complete administrative tasks associated with the role, including timesheets, daily diaries, checklists and inductions.
- Undertake all work in accordance with relevant quality, environmental and Work Health and Safety (WHS) requirements.
- Develop industry-recognised skills and knowledge through formal training and practical experience.
This position is based at Council's Works Depot and involves travel to sites across Lake Macquarie. Hours are 6:00am to 3:30pm, Tuesday to Friday, with occasional weekend work required with notice.
Read the position statement and capability framework to learn more.
WHAT WE OFFER
- Receive a wage whilst studying towards a qualification starting from $761.05 to $889.60 per week plus 12 per cent superannuation
- Earn while you learn, with all course fees fully funded and paid study time included.
- Receive an Adverse Working Conditions Allowance on top of your pay
- Grow your career, with annual pay reviews and opportunities for pay increases based on performance.
- Enjoy a 35-hour week and a four-day work week, giving you more time for the things you love.
- Four weeks paid annual leave each year.
- Learn from the best, working alongside experienced and qualified tradespeople who are committed to supporting your success.
- Access to a wide range of employee health, wellbeing and lifestyle benefits – click here for more.
ABOUT YOU
We're looking for motivated people who are eager to learn, enjoy working outdoors, and want to build a career in concreting.
To be successful, you'll have:
- Completion of Year 10 (Record of School Achievement) or equivalent, with satisfactory results in English and Mathematics.
- A White Card (Construction Induction Card) or the ability to obtain one before commencing.
- Current Provisional Drivers Licence
- Your dedicated and willing to undertake a Certificate III Concreting and within the term of the traineeship you are excited for this opportunity.
- You are customer focused with a passion and genuine interest in Concrete works
- Welcoming any challenge with your flexible approach with a positive work ethic and a "can-do" attitude.
- Being passionate about working together to meet a common goal you excel in a team environment.
- Stand out from the crowd with previous Concrete experience.
- You are a quick learner and eager to acquire knowledge and new skills
- Enjoy working in outdoor environment with ability to undertake physical requirements of the role
Please note: Applicants who have already completed a Certificate III in Concreting, or a higher-level qualification in a related field, may not be eligible for this apprenticeship.

Life at Fulton Hogan is about making the most of opportunities, taking responsibility, and making it happen. We don't stand still - there are always opportunities to do more and do better.

Our purpose of creating, connecting, and caring for communities is more than a saying to us - it's a way of thinking, working, and living because we're locals too, and seek to give back in ways that strengthen and build resilient communities. We do this because we genuinely care, enjoy what we do, and even manage to have some fun along the way! You'll find us partnering with local and national community groups, like Clontarf Foundation, and Black Dog Institute, in addition to indigenous groups and social enterprises, to ensure that our good work positively impacts and brings about sustainable change within our industry.
- Do we offer a 'competitive' salary package? Of course! Speak to our Talent Acquisition or People & Culture team to learn more.
What's on offer?
We are looking to build on our existing team with multiple experienced Site Engineers (Civil, Mechanical & Electrical) to work on key water infrastructure projects for Fulton Hogan Utilities. This is a fantastic opportunity for you to drive your career further within a vibrant delivery team that is proud to partner with our client to deliver world class utilities services for the customers and communities within which we operate.
In this role you'll be responsible for:
- Oversee daily construction activities and ensure work is carried out per the design and specifications
- Monitor site progress, ensure construction compliance in the field, working closely with site supervision and subcontractors
- With support from Project Engineers, management of project schedules, updating production plans and working to weekly and monthly schedules
- Assist with the development of Scope of Works and contracts for sub-contractors, managing and approvals of variations
- Attend and participate in HAZOPs, SiD reviews, CHAIR's and other workshops as required
- Manage the quality Lots, and ITP's during construction and commissioning stages.
How you'll connect to the role:
- A degree level qualification in Engineering (Civil or Mechanical or Electrical)
- Demonstrated previous experience in Site Engineering, working on construction projects in water infrastructure or utilities (preferred but not essential)
- Knowledge of project financial management, forecasting, procurement, design and contracts management functions
- A solid performer, with professional acumen and exceptional communication skills
- Adopting and driving Fulton Hogan's Living Safely 2.0 Culture.
Our people share the same set of values that keep us REAL. Respect, Energy and Effort, Attitude and Leadership encapsulate what we stand for at Fulton Hogan and encourage us to foster a diverse and inclusive culture where we listen to, care for, celebrate, and respect everyone.
We are committed to reconciliation and building and nurturing respectful relationships with First Nations peoples. Through our First Nations Engagement Strategy and Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP), we aim to promote opportunities, cultural understanding and partnerships that celebrate and acknowledge the contributions of Indigenous communities.
If our values resonate with you, please submit an application for the position.
For over 90 years, Fulton Hogan has been delivering high-quality infrastructure to improve the lives of people every day. Our 10,000+ team works in every kind of weather and environment, creating, connecting, and caring for communities across Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific.
